title: Google Gemini introduces Memory summary: New feature lets users check and delete details
summary: Google Gemini introduces Memory summary: New feature lets users check and delete details
detailed: Google is introducing a new feature into its Gemini AI assistant: the Memory summary, a feature for users to check and manage what the AI has remembered from previous interactions.
To view Memory summary in Gemini, navigate to Settings Menu > Memory > Memory Summary.
According to Google's support documentation, users should be at least 18 and logged into Google with their personal Google account.
Google is bringing visibility and editing into Gemini's personalisation system with Memory summary.
sentences: Google is introducing a new feature into its Gemini AI assistant: the Memory summary, a feature for users to check and manage what the AI has remembered from previous interactions.
The update lets users find out what their chatbot knows and update or delete information it may have stored that is incorrect or unwanted.
The feature builds on Gemini's existing memory capabilities, which help the assistant personalise responses using context from earlier interactions.
When using Memory summary, the user does not need to go through the various chats to comprehend what the assistant has remembered.
The new option groups stored data in files by category, such as personal background, location, relationships, work, interests, and preferences.
These sections can be opened and checked by the user to view information related to the user's account.
They may also edit each entry.
Details that don't fit the memory can be modified or removed.
For instance, if a person has switched jobs, relocated to another city or developed new tastes, they can change the information rather than an outdated fact affecting future answers.
Google has also introduced a memory change history.
This enables a user to monitor changes in information saved and view what changes have occurred over time in the user's memory information.
To view Memory summary in Gemini, navigate to Settings Menu > Memory > Memory Summary.
Users can access the feature on the Gemini app or on its website.

The user can browse the types of categories and edit/delete individual information with the controls provided.
The summary is designed to provide information saved for personalisation purposes, and is not intended to be a substitute for the account's wide-ranging activity controls.
According to Google's support documentation, users should be at least 18 and logged into Google with their personal Google account.
In the account settings, both 'Activity' and 'Memory' must be checked.
Users might not be able to get to the summary if either setting is turned off.
The supported region is currently "United States," and the available language is "English".
It also sets an active Google AI plan as a requirement.
The feature will be available on the Gemini mobile application and on the web version of the app (gemini.google.com).

Google is bringing visibility and editing into Gemini's personalisation system with Memory summary.

The feature is not a substitute for Keep Activity or other privacy settings for an account, but offers a direct means to review what the assistant has remembered, and to determine which information should be retained for future responses.
